lines.text: The Fields Medal's date has a typo.
Canadian mathematician J C Fields funded the gold medal.
A Canadian sculptor, R Tait McKenzie, designed it.
The front shows Archimedes and a motto about mastering the world.
The back shows his sphere inside a cylinder.
The date, 1933, is cut with an N where an M belongs.

lines.text: The first two medals went to Lars Ahlfors and Jesse Douglas.

post.caption: The Fields Medal's date has a typo. Canadian mathematician J C Fields funded the gold medal, and a Canadian sculptor, R Tait McKenzie, designed it. The front shows Archimedes and a motto about mastering the world. The date, 1933, is cut with an N where an M belongs. The first two medals went to Lars Ahlfors and Jesse Douglas. On his way to a new job, Ahlfors pawned his medal, and he joked it was the only Fields Medal held in a pawn shop. Every four years, it goes to mathematicians aged 40 or under.
